cards.text: Isaac, Abraham's son, is old now, and his eyes are so weak he can't see. He calls in his older son Esau and tells him he doesn't know the day of his death. Friend, back in that junk drawer I didn't know the day of the WEEK.

cards.question: Isaac has a job for Esau first. Esau grabs his quiver and bow and heads into the field. What's he sent out to do?

answers.text: Hunt some game for his father

cards.question: Isaac wants Esau to cook him a tasty dish he loves, so that he can ___ Esau before he dies.

cards.text: But somebody's listening. Rebekah, Isaac's wife, hears every word, like that coworker who is NOT listening to your phone call but somehow knows your whole weekend.
The second Esau heads out to hunt, Rebekah goes to her younger son, Jacob. She tells him everything she overheard.

cards.question: True or false: Rebekah tells Jacob to stay out of it and let Esau get the blessing.
Rebekah's got a plan, and she can cook what Isaac loves. What does she send Jacob out to the flock to get?

cards.text: She'll make the tasty dish Isaac loves, and Jacob carries it in so his father blesses HIM before he dies. One problem, and Jacob spots it right away.

cards.question: Jacob's about to walk in pretending to be his brother. What problem does Jacob see with the plan?

answers.text: Esau is hairy and he is smooth
Their father can still see a little
Esau will be home any minute

cards.question: Jacob worries that if his father touches him, he'll be found out as a deceiver and bring on himself a ___ instead of a ___.

cards.text: Rebekah doesn't even blink: "Your curse be on me, my son." And Jacob goes and gets the goats, and she makes the tasty food his father loves.

cards.question: The food's ready. Now Jacob has to pass for Esau. What does Rebekah put on Jacob first?
Good clothes, but Jacob is still smooth. What does Rebekah put on his hands and the smooth part of his neck?

cards.text: Rebekah hands Jacob the tasty food and the bread she made. Friend, the man is wearing GOAT on his NECK, and he's holding dinner like this is a totally normal family moment.
Jacob walks in and says, "My father." And Isaac asks the big one: "Which one are you, my son?"

cards.question: Moment of truth. What does Jacob tell his father, Isaac?

answers.text: I am Jacob your younger son
I am a servant sent by Esau

cards.text: Jacob tells Isaac to sit up and eat his game. Isaac can't see, but he can still read a TIMER: how did you find it so quickly, my son?

cards.question: Isaac wants to know how the hunt went so fast. What's Jacob's answer?

answers.text: The LORD your God brought it to me
The game walked right up to the tent
I found it waiting near the well

cards.text: Oh, he went THERE. He put the LORD's name on it, and Isaac still isn't sure, so he tells Jacob to come closer so he can touch him.

cards.question: Isaac touches him and says the voice is the voice of ___, but the hands are the hands of ___.

cards.text: Isaac doesn't recognize him, because his hands are hairy like Esau's. His EARS got it right, friend, and he went with the GOAT.

cards.question: True or false: Isaac asks one more time if this is really Esau, and Jacob finally comes clean.

cards.text: Jacob says, "I am." So Isaac eats the game, and Jacob brings him wine, and he drinks.

cards.question: True or false: Before the blessing, Isaac asks his son to come near and kiss him.

cards.text: Jacob kisses him, and Isaac smells his clothing, which is Esau's finest. Friend, this whole plan runs on borrowed laundry and a GOAT.

cards.question: Isaac starts blessing him. What does Isaac say the smell of his son is like?

answers.text: A field the LORD has blessed

cards.question: Isaac asks God to give his son the richness of the earth, with plenty of grain and new wine. What else does he ask for, from above?
True or false: In the blessing, Isaac says nations will bow down to this son, and so will the sons of his mother.
Isaac ends the blessing: may those who curse you be ___, and those who bless you be blessed.

cards.text: The blessing's done and Jacob's out the door, and THAT is when Esau gets back from the hunt. Friend, that's walking into the break room one second after somebody took the last cookie.

cards.question: True or false: Esau comes back from the hunt with nothing for his father.

cards.text: Esau tells his father to sit up and eat his game, so he can bless him. And Isaac's answer is three words: "Who are you?"

cards.question: Esau says he's Esau, the firstborn son. How does Isaac react?
True or false: Isaac tells Esau he can take back the blessing he already gave.

cards.text: Esau lets out a loud and bitter cry. "Bless me too, O my father!"

cards.question: What does Isaac tell Esau happened to his blessing?

answers.text: Your brother came deceitfully and took it
A stranger tricked me at the door
Your servant brought me the dish first

cards.text: Esau says Jacob is rightly named, because he's cheated him twice.

cards.question: Twice? Esau says Jacob took his ___, and now he's taken his blessing.

cards.text: Esau asks, "Haven’t you saved a blessing for me?" Isaac says he's already made Jacob his master and sustained him with grain and new wine, so what's left?

cards.question: Esau won't let it go. What does Esau ask his father next?

answers.text: Do you have only one blessing
Can you take the blessing back

cards.text: Then Esau weeps aloud. No joke here, friend. That's a grown man crying for his father's blessing.

cards.question: Jacob got the dew of heaven and the richness of the earth. Where does Isaac say Esau's home will be?

answers.text: Away from the richness of the land
Beside the waters of the Jordan

cards.question: Isaac tells Esau he will live by the ___ and serve his brother.
True or false: Isaac says Esau will serve his brother forever, with no way out.

cards.text: So when Esau rebels, he'll tear his brother's yoke off his neck. And friend, if you think these two brothers are done with each other, oh, we are NOT done.

findings.problem: The card calls Isaac "Abraham's son." That fact comes from outside Genesis 27:1-2, but the card gives no reference for it.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The setup says Esau grabs his quiver and bow. That rules out the wrong answers "Gather grain from the harvest" and "Draw water from the well," because nobody takes a bow to do either. The setup also says Esau grabs the weapons, but in v3 Isaac only tells him to take them.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Stop 1 card 1 already told the baker that Isaac "can't see." That rules out the wrong answer "Their father can still see a little."

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "reward" means nearly the same as "blessing" in blank 2. A baker could argue that "a curse instead of a reward" is right.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: This is a which-thing question, but the wrong answer "His father's old cloak" isn't a real detail from anywhere in the Bible. (The other wrong answer, "A robe of many colors," is.)

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.

findings.problem: The right answer, "The LORD your God brought it to me," sounds much more like the Bible than the casual wrong answers ("The game walked right up to the tent"). That makes it stand out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The statement says Isaac asks for the kiss "Before the blessing," and its answer is True. But v23 already says "so he blessed him" before the kiss in v26, so a baker could argue that False, the wrong answer, is right.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: "Isaac asks God to give his son…" turns Isaac's blessing ("May God give to you…") into a request to God. The text calls it a blessing spoken to his son.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The statement says Isaac says nations "will bow down." Verse 29 words it as a wish: "May peoples serve you and nations bow down to you… may the sons of your mother bow down to you."

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "He falls fast asleep" is silly next to a father finding out he's been deceived.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The right answer, "Away from the richness of the land," is a description, while the wrong answers are named places (the Jordan, Goshen). The right answer also repeats "richness" from the setup, so it stands out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The setup says "Jacob got the dew of heaven and the richness of the earth." That states as a fact what Isaac spoke as a blessing ("May God give to you…").

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.
